    #7195. Bilt Seeks An $18 Billion Valuation — The Business Behind Its Jennifer Lopez Concert Goes Far Beyond Rent

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 25m • 📚 Deep Dive (4915 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Bilt Seeks An $18 Billion Valuation — The Business Behind Its Jennifer Lopez Concert Goes Far Beyond Rent

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4915 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that bilt is reportedly seeking to raise $500 million at an $18 billion valuation.
    • Recent findings suggest that last week Bilt held a dinner for 400 people in the two thousand year old Egyptian Temple of Dendur inside the Metropolitan Museum of Art, with food led by Thomas Keller and Daniel Boulud and a private Jennifer Lopez concert.
    • Recent findings suggest that consumers see the side of the business that’s relevant to them.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that bilt is reportedly seeking to raise $500 million at an $18 billion valuation. That would be roughly two-thirds higher than the $10.75 billion valuation from its last funding round in 2025. They’re asking investors to back a company that wants to influence where people eat, shop, travel and spend their time, starting with the relationship it built through paying rent. Last week Bilt held a dinner for 400 people in the two thousand year old Egyptian Temple of Dendur inside the Metropolitan Museum of Art, with food led by Thomas Keller and Daniel Boulud and a private Jennifer Lopez concert. Ken Chenault, Roger Goodell and Barry Sternlicht were some of the business leaders speaking. The event launched their ‘NeighborhoodOS’ platform. And that provides real insight into the actual Bilt business, where rewards are just one piece of it. Jennifer Lopez’s video from the Met performance Consumers see the side of the business that’s relevant to them. Most people won’t ever view it as anything other than rewards for rent, or a credit card, and that’s fine. The merchant side doesn’t need to understand the travel rewards piece, either. But in case you want a window into what’s really going on, here’s an attempt at an explanation. J. Lo held a private concert at this dinner. I often see remarks on Reddit about how Bilt spends money each month on celebrities hosting its Rent Day, basically seeing that transaction as payment to market Bilt to them (or as just wasted money). That misses half of it. Bilt’s CEO explained the J. Lo relationship, “We agreed to help do the relaunch of her new album.” There’s huge value to the celebrity in being featured in front of Bilt’s audience. The financial terms probably vary with each one, but Bilt gains attention from the celebrity and the celebrity gains access to Bilt’s audience. You often see celebrities with something to promote, like J. Lo’s new album. We naturally see ourselves as the customers being rewarded. Our attention and spending are also what Bilt brings to its partners. That’s how it can negotiate rewards for us. Businesses spend money trying to reach customers, and a rewards program returns some of that money to the people whose business they’re trying to attract. The scale of Bilt’s ambitions are pretty massive. Bilt is trying to eat the world. Or at least a meaningful share of the $6.6 trillion in annual U.S. retail and food services spending it indicates happens in person. Their business began with a really insightful way to find good customers – reach into their homes, process their rent and get them signed up. Bilt’s latest company announcement says its platform reaches approximately one in four U.S. apartment buildings and expects to process more than $100 billion in housing payments this year. They report more than 8.2 million members and over $12 billion in rewarded spending at local merchants over the past year. Rewarded spending isn’t necessarily spending Bilt caused, but it’s a substantial base of transactions to build their platform off us. As I wrote earlier this year, move-in is a particularly valuable moment. Someone needs a coffee shop, gym, pharmacy and regular place for dinner. Their habits are up for grabs. Acquiring that relationship through their home gives Bilt a chance to influence years of spending. The early audience was especially attractive. In a 2024 interview, its head of loyalty Dave Canty (ex-Starwood, IHG, JetBlue) described core customers aged 24–34, a median age around 29 and average income around $147,000. That made it easier to sign on initial partners who wanted access to the young professionals Bilt was reaching. Airlines start with people who want their miles already sitting on their planes. An independent rewards program has to find its own reason for customers to join. Bilt found one in an expense nearly everyone has, and where there wasn’t competition in offering rewards for their transactions. They offered property owners stickiness as well as a better payment processing platform. American Express’s Plenti had significant merchants and their customers, but never established a compelling enough new relationship to change spending. It closed in 2018. Coalition rewards have achieved some scale abroad, including Air Miles in Canada and Nectar in Britain. The challenge is making the common program worth choosing over whatever customers already do. Bilt has better tools for that than a small rebate. I consider its points the most valuable transferable currency. A restaurant’s standalone rewards might never accumulate into anything I care about. Combine them with points from housing and other spending, and they can contribute to a Hyatt stay or an international business class award. A restaurant wants nearby customers who spend well and return. It also needs to handle reservations, remember guests, deliver good service and get paid without wasting staff time. Neighborhood OS connects systems the restaurant already uses. OpenTable’s new partnership puts guest information into its table management system and brings personalized offers into the OpenTable app. The restaurant can send an offers to people who’ve just moved nearby and manage offers for regulars – their own loyalty platform. OpenTable reports that participating restaurants have seen: Average checks up to 18% higher among Bilt members than other guests. Table turns reduced by up to 11 minutes on average. Higher average bills may be Bilt’s customer base being higher spending, or they may be encouraging higher spend. That’s not clear. But their technology does seem to speed up paying and leaving, which means serving more guests per table. Bilt’s mobile checkout lets diners tap or scan a receipt card, view the check, split it and pay in a browser. You can leave when you’re finished without waiting for someone to take your credit card and bring it back. Removing dead time after a meal gives the guest back their evening and makes the table available sooner. When there’s demand for another seating, a restaurant can generate more revenue from the same space. Keller and Boulud’s involvement extends beyond preparing food for a launch dinner. In Bilt’s March hospitality announcement, Keller described learning who guests are before they arrive. Boulud talked about inviting wine enthusiasts to wine events and cocktail enthusiasts to cocktail events. Connecting reservations, preferences, past visits and payments helps a restaurant recognize more people than an owner can personally remember. The restaurant can also deliver an experience through other Bilt partners. At Block’s investor day last year, Bilt’s President and Chief Revenue Officer Brandt Smallwood described automating drinks after a third visit, as well as benefits such as dessert or a free Lyft ride at the end of the meal. A ride home can be part of the restaurant’s hospitality, with Bilt doing the work connecting the businesses. The customer doesn’t need to understand the systems behind it. They get recognized, something arrives at their table, and their ride is arranged. That’s different from getting an email with a coupon code to remember next time. There’s also less work for employees. A Google Cloud case study describes Bilt’s concierge moving a reservation and adjusting party size through the underlying systems. It reports about 95% of member conversations handled without a human handoff, up from 86% six months earlier. More partners also means more ways to fund the benefits. Bilt’s acquisition of Banyan brought technology for reading individual items on receipts. A consumer brand can reward the purchase of its product rather than merely knowing someone spent $80 at a store or restaurant. A restaurant supplies a complimentary appetizer, a brand funds a product promotion, a landlord, hotel chain or sports partner funds a member benefit – Bilt connects the offer, the targeted customer and the transaction, and does so in a way no small merchant could accomplish on their own. Constellation Brands is participating, bringing Modelo Especial and Corona Extra benefits to customers across sports fandoms, residential communities, offices and local businesses. A national brand’s marketing budget can help make a neighborhood membership more valuable. An appetizer can cost less to provide than the guest values it. An empty table on Tuesday has different economics from the last table on Saturday. Bilt can help direct incentives to the places and times where they create more business, then show the merchant which offers led to visits and spending. Bilt is also white labeling its membership technology. A sports team can reward fans between games and a hotel program can be useful when a member is home. The organization keeps its customer relationship while Bilt supplies connections to businesses where those customers spend. Some of the expansion is already being bought or distributed through partners: The confirmed $300 million LAVA acquisition is supposed to bring relationships with 56 professional sports franchises and more than 300 connections to existing technology systems. Bilt is buying access to audiences and the ability to deliver benefits through ticketing, payments and other systems. Capillary’s planned integration offers a route to clients of an established loyalty provider serving more than 450 brands, including Hertz, Shell and PUMA. Kastle’s partnership would let 60,000 business building access customers offer employee memberships combining office access with neighborhood benefits, like a nearby dry cleaning credit or a team happy hour. Marriott, Hyatt, the Phoenix Suns, Houston Rockets, Houston Texans and Sacramento Kings have been announced as membership partners. Broader integrations roll out starting next year. Verifone, Fiserv, Adyen and OpenTable provide another route into businesses through systems they already use. That gives Bilt distribution on both sides. It can reach consumers through organizations they already belong to and merchants through suppliers they already work with. A competing program would have to assemble enough of both in the same places. And each of these pieces is hard on their own. Bilt earns money from housing and resident technology, merchant commissions, its card business and now additional software subscriptions. Its restaurant pricing is $495 a month for Neighborhood OS plus $195 for Neighborhood Marketplace ($690 combined). Software income from merchant tools gives it another way to make money. I don’t use all their partners but I do use Lyft and Grubhub, and I redeem with Blacklane and BLADE. I book travel through their portal. And their Palladium card is my daily driver. Palladium gets most of my spending and I’ve chosen to preserve 4% Bilt Cash earning. They’ll pry that option from my cold dead hands. (The option offering up to 1.25 points per dollar on housing is what most people choose anyway and still leaves a very good card once 4% back in Bilt Cash goes away for new cardmembers.) Still, my experience isn’t the experience of every member. Bilt told Thrifty Traveler that fewer than 10% of members have its credit card. Someone whose landlord uses Bilt may pay rent through it and do little else. Founder Ankur Jain has called the card “less than 11%” of Bilt’s business (without defining the denominator). That’s not surprising. Delta says roughly one-third of active SkyMiles members carry a cobrand card (without defining ‘active’), while its American Express relationship is on track to generate more than $9 billion this year. But it means that there are also likely a lot of members who don’t transact with Bilt frequently, outside of paying rent. Daily Rewards debuts January 15 and looks designed to develop more of that engagement.     Recent findings suggest that J. Lo held a private concert at this dinner. Lo relationship, “We agreed to help do the relaunch of her upcoming album.” There’s huge value to the celebrity in being featured in front of Bilt’s audience. The financial terms probably vary with each one, but Bilt gains attention from the celebrity and the celebrity gains access to Bilt’s audience. You often see celebrities with something to promote, like J. Lo’s new album.

    Sources indicate that we naturally see ourselves as the customers being rewarded. Our attention and spending are also what Bilt brings to its partners. That’s how it can negotiate rewards for us. Businesses spend money trying to reach customers, and a rewards program returns some of that money to the people whose business they’re trying to attract.

    In a recent development, the scale of Bilt’s ambitions are pretty massive. Bilt is trying to eat the world. Or at least a meaningful share of the $6.6 trillion in annual U.S. retail and food services spending it says happens in person.

    Their business began with a really insightful way to find good customers – reach into their homes, process their rent and get them signed up. Bilt’s latest manufacturer announcement says its platform reaches approximately one in four U.S. apartment buildings and expects to process more than $100 billion in housing payments this year.

    They report more than 8.2 million members and over $12 billion in rewarded spending at local merchants over the past year. Rewarded spending isn’t necessarily spending Bilt caused, but it’s a substantial base of transactions to build their platform off us.

    It has been revealed that as I wrote earlier this year, move-in is a particularly valuable moment. Someone needs a coffee shop, gym, pharmacy and regular place for dinner. Their habits are up for grabs. Acquiring that relationship through their home gives Bilt a chance to influence years of spending.

    It has been revealed that the early audience was especially attractive. In a 2024 interview, its head of loyalty Dave Canty (ex-Starwood, IHG, JetBlue) described core customers aged 24–34, a median age around 29 and average income around $147,000. That made it easier to sign on initial partners who wanted access to the young professionals Bilt was reaching.

    Sources indicate that airlines start with people who want their miles already sitting on their planes. An independent rewards program has to find its own reason for customers to join. Bilt found one in an expense nearly everyone has, and where there wasn’t competition in offering rewards for their transactions. They offered property owners stickiness as well as a better payment processing platform.

    Industry observers note that american Express’s Plenti had big merchants and their customers, but never established a compelling enough fresh relationship to change spending. It closed in 2018. Coalition rewards have achieved some scale abroad, including Air Miles in Canada and Nectar in Britain. The challenge is making the common program worth choosing over whatever customers already do.

    Bilt has better tools for that than a small rebate. I consider its points the most valuable transferable currency. A restaurant’s standalone rewards might never accumulate into anything I care about. Combine them with points from housing and other spending, and they can contribute to a Hyatt stay or an international business class award.

OpenTable’s newly introduced partnership puts guest information into its table management system and brings personalized offers into the OpenTable app. The restaurant can send an offers to people who’ve just moved nearby and manage offers for regulars – their own loyalty platform.

    #7193. The Plot to Overthrow the Electoral College Must Fail

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1608 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nationalreview ↗ Open Full Page

    The Plot to Overthrow the Electoral College Must Fail

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1608 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that article II, Section 1 of the Constitution sets out the process by which Americans select their president.
    • Democrats have been railing against the Electoral College since losing the 2000 and 2016 elections while winning a plurality of the popular vote.
    • Industry observers note that A proposed workaround has sailed through the legislatures of 18 blue states and the District of Columbia: the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that article II, Section 1 of the Constitution sets out the process by which Americans select their president. Alexander Hamilton marveled at the time, in Federalist No. 68, that it was “almost the only part of the system, of any consequence, which has escaped without severe censure, or which has received the slightest mark of approbation from its opponents.” The core of that process is that the members of the Electoral College are selected in each state. With only the Twelfth Amendment’s modification in 1804 to adjust how the vice president is selected, this same system has been in continuous use for 238 years. It is how George Washington, Abraham Lincoln, Franklin D. Roosevelt, Ronald Reagan, and Barack Obama were elected. Now, a nefarious plot aims to overthrow the American system.

    Democrats have been railing against the Electoral College since losing the 2000 and 2016 elections while winning a plurality of the popular vote. These partisan sour grapes have often been dismissed as empty talk because the Electoral College is established by the Constitution, so only an amendment could abolish it. An amendment requires a two-thirds vote of Congress and the consent of 38 states, both of which are out of reach on a party-line vote.

    Industry observers note that A proposed workaround has sailed through the legislatures of 18 blue states and the District of Columbia: the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact. The theory is that these states would award their electors not to the winner of the popular vote in their own state, but to the winner of the national popular vote. It may be that a state can decide on its own to do this. States have not always picked electors by statewide popular vote. Many states at the Founding had their state legislatures choose electors. South Carolina did so all the way to the Civil War. Colorado in 1876 was the last state to do so, but only because it had just been admitted to statehood and claimed not to have time to organize a statewide vote. Other states have awarded electors to the winners of each House district, as Maine and Nebraska do today; this system was upheld by the Supreme Court in 1892.

    But the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact is not just a unilateral decision by individual states about how to award their electors. If it had been, it would already have been effective in 2024, and Donald Trump would have won the Electoral College 530–8 with 49.7 percent of the popular vote. Instead, it is styled as an agreement that goes into effect only if states composing a majority of the Electoral College approve it. At present, the signatories control 222 electoral votes. With Democrats gaining trifectas in Pennsylvania, Michigan, Wisconsin, Nevada, and Arizona, they conceivably could pass the compact in states controlling 283 electoral votes. They also now control the Fresh Hampshire state legislature, although with a veto-proof majority only in one of its two chambers, they would have to get through Republican Governor Kelly Ayotte.

    Sources indicate that passage is not certain. Michigan Democrats have previously rejected the compact in 2023 and 2024, and in Nevada (a smaller state that would be swamped under the compact), the Democratic governor vetoed it in 2019. Some of the small-state signatories, such as Delaware, Vermont, Rhode Island, or Upcoming Mexico, might yet have second thoughts now that they are playing with live ammunition.

    Recent findings suggest that moreover, under Article I, Section 10, interstate compacts require the consent of Congress. Even if Democrats passed it in the next two years with the aim of changing the rules for the 2028 election, Trump would surely veto it. After the 2030 Census, a number of the signatory states are expected to lose House seats, which will further narrow the margin for keeping it in effect. Then, there’s the question of whether the Supreme Court would allow individual states to gang up and effectively nullify the entire constitutional design of our presidential election system.

    Industry observers note that legal obstacles aside, this is a bad idea. To start with, the very durability of our system over such a long period is an argument in its favor. No other nation has used the same system for choosing its head of state and government for so long. Leaving aside the dubious precedents of 1824 (when popular vote records were not kept in the most populous state) and 1876 (when fraud was rampant in both parties and Southern Democrats engaged in mass violence against Republican voters), the Electoral College has only delivered a different outcome from the national popular vote three times in our history. In each case, the national vote was fairly close and neither candidate got a popular majority, so the Electoral College provided the legitimacy of a majority result that the popular vote could not. This may have frustrated Californians, but it was not just the tyranny of a few small places with no people in them. In 2016, Trump won the popular vote in seven of the ten largest states. It is nearly impossible to win a national popular majority without carrying the Electoral College.

    We have an Electoral College because we are a nation of diverse and distinct states. The American people are long accustomed to this system. The people ratified the Constitution and its amendments state-by-state. The Senate is elected by the people in states, the House by people in districts. Both political parties choose their presidential nominees by primary elections in each state. Americans have never before held a nationwide popular vote for any purpose. Our election systems, run by state and local officials with a variety of rules for the timing of casting and counting ballots and for confirming the qualifications of voters, are not designed for such a vote.

    According to recent reports, our campaigns today still prioritize appeals to the most closely divided states. This encourages presidential candidates to pitch at least some of their message to voters in the center, and also to travel the country in order to garner coverage in statewide media and the support of state and local power brokers. A national popular vote campaign would drive us even further down the road of nationalizing the campaign media environment and encouraging candidates to rally voters in their party’s strongholds. It would also exacerbate the divide between urban and rural or small-town America, given how the largest cities could effectively ally themselves against their own in-state neighbors.

    Few of the world’s democracies conduct a nationwide vote for the chief executive. In France, which is one of those, the first man to win such a vote seized power in a coup before his first term ended. National popular plebiscites are far more common in dictatorial systems, where the president has more control over who counts the votes. One of the reasons why the January 6 mob was never a serious threat to overturn the 2020 election was that the state-by-state winners had already been publicly certified in 50 separate state capitals. This was a deliberate feature of the system: As Hamilton wrote, “as the electors, chosen in each State, are to assemble and vote in the State in which they are chosen, this detached and divided situation will expose them much less to heats and ferments . . . than if they were all to be convened at one time, in one place.”.

    We would inevitably need to overhaul our entire election system to accommodate a nationwide vote. It is not a coincidence that such a nationalization of elections is favored by many of the same people who want to do away with the Electoral College. As things stand today, the whole country would have to wait on California, which not only takes weeks to count votes, but does so in order to count late-arriving ballots and to “cure” defective ballots — a process bound to erode confidence in a close election. That matters little when nobody doubts the outcome in California. But by making elections turn on the margins of victory in the deepest-blue or deepest-red jurisdictions, whose election officials are uniformly of the same party, the incentives for all manner of electoral malfeasance would be supercharged.

    In a recent development, the 1888 election provides a vivid, if extreme, example of how the Electoral College limits the scope of mischief done by the corruption of voting systems in particular states. The eleven states of the former Confederacy were then well into the post-Reconstruction suppression of the black vote in their states. As a result, the Democratic nominee, Grover Cleveland, won those states by almost 25 points, with over 60 percent of the vote. This propelled Cleveland to a narrow plurality in the national popular vote even though his Republican opponent, Benjamin Harrison, won a popular majority in the rest of the country. Yet the Electoral College gave Harrison the victory because his support was not as concentrated in an unrepresentative handful of states in which the vote was compromised.

    If a nationwide vote would be a headache, a nationwide recount would be a nightmare. Nobody who lived through the 2000 and 2020 post-election controversies should have any illusions that such a thing could be conducted in a civil and orderly fashion in today’s America. Rather than wait to learn that lesson the hard way, we should step back from the brink of overthrowing the system that has chosen our nation’s leader from the beginning.

    The Editors comprise the senior editorial staff of National Review magazine and nationalreview.com.

    On “The Plot to Overthrow the Electoral College Must Fail”.

    Rove is launching personalized shopping offers of up to 25 miles per dollar on November 20. Connect your card accounts, activate an offer, and the program can give you a higher earning rate based on your shopping history.

    If you buy from Nike, Adidas may be willing to spend real money to win your next purchase. That’s the example I reported from Rove’s presentation at the oneworld Loyalty Summit in September. CEO Max Morganroth described targeted merchant commissions reaching 40%. This puts that pitch in front of consumers, with an established advertising company helping supply the offers.

    Recent findings suggest that rove says members will find personalized offers in the ‘For You’ section of its website and app after connecting their card accounts. Enhanced offers will display the standard earning rate alongside the higher rate.

    They’re also expanding in-store earning to hundreds of participating physical retailers. Activate an eligible offer before buying, pay with the connected card, and the purchase gets tracked when the charge clears. Rove indicates miles will typically post within seven days.

    These are selected offers reaching up to 25x, and Rove tells me merchants can change from month to month, and the same merchant might offer one person 5x and another 20x depending on whom it wants to reach.

    Sources indicate that rove began rolling out in-store shopping alongside its app, dining program and instant gift card rewards in August. The newly introduced pieces are the personalized enhanced rates and broader retail coverage.

    In a recent development, A shopping portal generally earns a commission for sending a merchant a sale. Better targeting can make that referral worth more.

    Sources indicate that someone who regularly spends money in a category, but buys from a competitor, is a prospect worth reaching. So is someone who used to shop at a store and stopped. A merchant might pay to bring that person back, get an occasional customer to make another visit, or encourage a larger purchase.

    The best prospect isn’t necessarily the biggest spender. It’s the person whose spending the offer can profitably change. Adidas gains little from paying a committed Adidas customer a huge rebate on shoes they were already going to buy. And it doesn’t much from showing a Nike loyalist an offer they’ll never use.

    According to recent reports, rewards provider Valuedynamx describes a retailer campaign that gave new shoppers stronger incentives, lapsed shoppers offers to bring them back, and loyal customers smaller rewards. Its case study reports a 20.2% incremental sales lift among lapsed customers and 13.3% among new ones.

    Recent findings suggest that targeting also lets a brand offer a substantial rebate without cutting the public price for everyone. It can spend more to win a customer it wants while avoiding an expensive storewide sale.

    Cardlytics unveiled its Rove partnership on October 6, giving Rove access to its offers program. Rove brings an audience motivated by travel rewards. Cardlytics brings merchant campaigns and purchase-based targeting.

    Rove’s program terms name Cardlytics and Plaid. Members can connect eligible debit or credit accounts through Plaid, and Cardlytics uses account transactions for targeting, reporting and measurement. Rove tells me its partners process the last 24 months of transaction history so merchants can target offers. Rove itself claims it neither stores nor interacts with that history.

    That history can reveal which merchants you use, how recently you’ve shopped, how often you return and how much you spend.

    The policy also states Rove’s browser extension matches participating stores locally and doesn’t transmit your browsing history.

    Industry observers note that for the Cardlytics offers, personal identifiers are removed, but permit aggregated marketing insights, transaction-level validation and licensing transaction data to partners. Bilt’s neighborhood rewards and airline dining programs are other familiar ways to earn from merchant relationships using cards you already have.     #7191. American officially retires its most exclusive long-haul seat: Bittersweet or overdue?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (785 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thepointsguy ↗ Open Full Page

    American officially retires its most exclusive long-haul seat: Bittersweet or overdue?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This week, the carrier (officially) bid farewell to Flagship First international service.
    • We’ve been talking for years about American’s aims to retire its international-style first-class product.
    • The airline is replacing Flagship First with larger and more modern business-class cabins on its marquee planes — cabins that will feature its next-generation Flagship Suites.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It’s the end of an era at American Airlines.

    This week, the carrier (officially) bid farewell to Flagship First international service.

    We’ve been talking for years about American’s aims to retire its international-style first-class product.

    The airline is replacing Flagship First with larger and more modern business-class cabins on its marquee planes — cabins that will feature its next-generation Flagship Suites.

    For a lot of flyers, that’s likely to be a positive shift: It will mean a host of upgrades in business-class, including seats with sliding privacy doors and superior tech.

    But there’s at least a little nostalgia in bidding farewell to a cabin that, for many years, was billed as American’s most exclusive.

    American was the last U.S. airline that claimed to offer a standalone, international first-class product.

    Across the global airline industry, many carriers sunset long-haul first-class years ago, choosing to instead offer more — and improved — business-class seats, which take up less space and are considered more profitable.

    For years, Delta Air Lines’ Delta One business-class suites have been its premier long-haul offering.

    United Airlines bid farewell to international first class in 2018 when it pivoted to Polaris business class.

    That left American’s Flagship First as a relic, of sorts, in the U.S. airline industry — and even on its own planes.

    In recent years, you could only find the cabin on two fleet types American operated: its Boeing 777-300ER, which offered eight of the pods up front in their own dedicated cabin.

    Plus, AA still (for now) offers Flagship First on its three-cabin Airbus A321T, which has been a fixture on lucrative coast-to-coast routes like New York to Los Angeles and San Francisco.

    But soon, it will be a thing of the past on both planes.

    American is retrofitting its larger 777s, ditching first-class in favor of 70 all-new Flagship Suites in business-class — along with the biggest premium economy cabin it’s ever offered.

    Related: This is now American Airlines' most premium plane: Here's what it's like on board.

    On domestic routes, the A321T will actually keep flying with Flagship First through March 28.

    But after that, AA will stop selling the Flagship First cabin on the A321T configuration, which is eventually going away as American flexes in its fresh A321XLR planes fully onto its top cross-country flights.

    In a lot of ways, American ditching Flagship First is a positive (and arguably overdue) transition for flyers.

    It’ll give passengers more lie-flat seats to pick from, whether they’re paying cash, using AAdvantage miles or using a systemwide upgrade.

    Also — while those Flagship First seats were really spacious and comfortable, many would say that American's new business-class product is a major upgrade from what it previously offered in that cabin.

    On some planes, that even includes extra-spacious Flagship Suites Preferred in the front and bulkhead rows of some planes, which offer a lot more space.

    Value check: Is it worth buying up to American Airlines' new business-class Flagship Suite Preferred?

    Beyond the aircraft, American also prepares to still offer many of the same amenities for business-class that first-class passengers historically enjoyed.

    For instance, its Flagship business-class tickets get access to its premium lounges. Passengers traveling in Flagship Business and Flagship Business Plus on qualifying international, transcontinental and Hawaii routes will also be able to have a meal in its exclusive restaurant-style dining rooms in Dallas, Los Angeles and Miami.

    The experience is available on a space-available basis.

    So, in some ways, you could argue the end of Flagship First is more symbolic than anything.

    But for some AA loyalists, it's still a little bittersweet.

    TPG’s Clint Henderson is our resident Flagship First enthusiast, having flown the cabin on dozens of occasions.

    "The service in first class wasn't particularly differentiated, but I still liked a few of the special touches," he said, pointing to the additional soup course and appetizer, along with a handful of elevated amenities.

    He especially appreciated the “La-Z-Boy-style” seats at the front of American’s 777s, which could lie flat or swivel and turn into an “office in the sky.”.

    “While these cabins are definitely showing their age,” Henderson added, “I’m sad to see it go.”.

    While Flagship First is technically going away as an official cabin on international service, the seats themselves won't disappear overnight.

    Recent findings suggest that so far, American has only retrofitted one of its 20 Boeing 777-300ERs that feature the seats. That means a handful of jets with the old first-class seats will still be flying around well into 2027.

    Going forward, the former Flagship First seats on those planes will be marketed as business-class. They won’t come with the full first-class service, but you’ll still get the elevated seat.

    Luxury Tours Pushed Deeper Into Amazon As Gateways Urbanize

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (215 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Skift

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As luxury Amazon trips grow in popularity, operators are having to go further to deliver what they sell: remoteness.
    • As luxury Amazon trips grow in popularity, tourism is adding pressure to the very thing it’s sold on: remote, authentic experiences.
    • Tour operators increasingly define luxury as access to remote locations and unique experiences.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Photo Credit: Hans Schwarzkopf/Pixabay.

    As luxury Amazon trips grow in popularity, operators are having to go further to deliver what they sell: remoteness. Gateway cities, including Brazil’s Manaus, are sprawling, and lodges that once felt remote no longer are.

    As luxury Amazon trips grow in popularity, tourism is adding pressure to the very thing it’s sold on: remote, authentic experiences.

    Tour operators increasingly define luxury as access to remote locations and unique experiences. As the industry grows, the gateways to these experiences, and especially to the Amazon in Brazil, are becoming more urbanized — threatening the very thing travelers are there to experience.

    Industry observers note that one notable pressure point is waterways. CroisiEurope will debut luxury cruises from Brazil to Colombia next year, and Carnival Corporation’s Seabourn revealed a fresh cruise featuring Amazon river sailing for 2028. Lindblad also chartered a 42-guest ship to expand its presence in the Amazon for this year, doubling its capacity, and Ponant bought a majority stake in Aqua Expeditions, which runs Peruvian river cruises.

    Amazonastur, the tourism agency in Brazil’s Amazonas state, expects to see 17,000 visitors including crew.

    Tour Associations Attempt to Take On Package Emissions Reporting

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (252 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Skift

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that A common framework makes it easier for operators to benchmark against one another and their suppliers, but the burden still falls on operators to collect and crunch the numbers.
    • According to recent reports, in 2026, hotels tend to report emissions on a per-room basis, trains report per passenger, and a bus tech giant reports its emissions for the whole vehicle.
    • According to recent reports, two tour operator associations have developed a website they hope can help solve this problem.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Photo Credit: Oleg Mityukhin from Pixabay.

    It has been revealed that A common framework makes it easier for operators to benchmark against one another and their suppliers, but the burden still falls on operators to collect and crunch the numbers. The best way to get tour operators to calculate their emissions would be releasing a tool to do it for them.

    According to recent reports, in 2026, hotels tend to report emissions on a per-room basis, trains report per passenger, and a bus tech giant reports its emissions for the whole vehicle. From these fragmented data points, a package tour operator has to fold all of those numbers into one to understand its climate impact.

    According to recent reports, two tour operator associations have developed a website they hope can help solve this problem. The idea is to simplify emissions calculations for package tour operators by bringing resources into one place.

    The site, called TEMPO, is the work of the European Tourism Association (ETOA) and United States Tour Operators Association (USTOA). It points to free methodologies operators can use to measure emissions and to free calculation tools for each part of a tour, as well as identifying when one doesn’t exist.

    “A tour operator has to piece together data from many suppliers, each measuring a different service in a different unit,” ETOA’s director gene.

    Per Politico, the incoming speaker of the House, Hakeem Jeffries, wishes to massively increase federal entitlements:.

    Industry observers note that I’m sorry: What? What is Jeffries talking about? Have he and those praising him taken leave of their senses? The United States is $41 trillion in debt. The federal government is running annual deficits of $2 trillion. We paid more in interest last year than we spent on defense. Medicare is unsustainable as it is. Social Security is just six years away from mandatory benefit cuts. And the Democratic Party’s leader in the House wants to add a vast new spending program onto the pile. Do my eyes deceive me?

    #7185. Bilt Offers JetBlue Elite Status For December Rent Day—With A Fast Track To Keep It Through 2027

    Bilt Offers JetBlue Elite Status For December Rent Day—With A Fast Track To Keep It Through 2027

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 50 min read (10049 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~50 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that bilt’s December Rent Day offers a three month trial of JetBlue elite status, with a much easier path to keeping it through January 2028.
    • According to recent reports, when Bilt added JetBlue as a transfer partner last month, I wrote that status matches could be coming.
    • Industry observers note that there’s also up to a 100% bonus redeeming Bilt points for credit card statement credits, a targeted spending offer, and Brittany Snow playing Rent Free.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that bilt’s December Rent Day offers a three month trial of JetBlue elite status, with a much easier path to keeping it through January 2028. Silver and Gold members get Mosaic 1 at no points cost. Platinum members start at Mosaic 2, which means EvenMore seats at booking instead of waiting until closer to departure. When Bilt added JetBlue as a transfer partner last month, I wrote that status matches could be coming. You qualify based on your Bilt status, so you don’t need to bring elite status from another airline. There’s also up to a 100% bonus redeeming Bilt points for credit card statement credits, a targeted spending offer, and Brittany Snow playing Rent Free. I have no idea who she is. I’m much more interested in the JetBlue offer than cashing out Bilt points at under 1.5 cents apiece. Three Months Of JetBlue Status, With A Path Through January 2028 Here’s the initial status offered: Bilt Status   JetBlue Trial Status   Points Requirement Blue Mosaic 1 10,000 Bilt points Silver Mosaic 1 None Gold Mosaic 1 None Platinum Mosaic 2 None Blue members have to transfer 10,000 points to trigger the match. Everyone has three months after receiving the matched status to earn and receive enough qualifying tiles to extend it through January 31, 2028: Status Earned   Challenge Requirement   Normal Annual Requirement Mosaic 1 10 tiles 50 tiles Mosaic 2 25 tiles 100 tiles Mosaic 3 40 tiles 150 tiles Under JetBlue’s normal earning rules, a tile takes $100 in qualifying spending on flights, JetBlue Vacations or TrueBlue Travel, or $1,000 in JetBlue credit card spending. So the travel equivalents are $1,000, $2,500 and $4,000. Taxes and fees don’t count. The corresponding spend amounts would be $10,000, $25,000 and $40,000, or you could combine tiles from travel and card spending. Spending on a Bilt card isn’t JetBlue card spending. You can earn JetBlue tiles via travel on JetBlue, United Airlines, JetBlue Vacations; cobrand card spend; purchased or earned bonus tiles (but gifted tiles don’t count); and the annual 25 Tile Bonus awarded to JetBlue Premier Wcardmembers. Folks who have received a past JetBlue challenge are eligible for this offer. Where The Status Is Most Useful The immediate value is better seating and fewer fees on trips you already intend to take. Mosaic 1 includes one checked bag, priority services, eligible same-day switches, and complimentary EvenMore selection starting 36 hours before departure for the member and up to two companions, subject to availability. Mosaic 2 adds a second checked bag and moves EvenMore selection to booking for the member and up to two companions. Mosaic 3 includes four Premium Upgrade Certificates, the upcoming name for Move to Mint certificates (and those meeting the challenge requirements will receive them). Main Base fares exclude vital seating benefits. And Mosaic 1 through 3 don’t include Mosaic 4 lounge access. JetBlue has also revealed complimentary upgrades to its new BlueFirst domestic first class for all Mosaic tiers as equipped aircraft enter service. These are space available upgrades, with higher Mosaic levels ahead of lower ones. Main Base and EvenMore Base fares don’t qualify. Premium Upgrade Certificates can confirm Mint or BlueFirst, including on eligible TrueBlue points tickets. Four certificates don’t necessarily mean four upgrades because the number required varies by flight. Starting February 1, JetBlue will also let Mosaic 2 members select a certificate through Perks You Pick. I’ve asked whether matched members get that selection. There’s A United Airlines Angle, Too Under JetBlue’s Blue Sky partnership, Mosaic members receive benefits on eligible United Airlines trips booked through JetBlue, including a checked bag, preferred seats after booking and Economy Plus at check-in. Mosaic 1 gets Group 2 boarding, while Mosaic 2 and above get Group 1. United flights booked through JetBlue also earn tiles under the ordinary program. So you can keep JetBlue status through travel on United. There’s No Transfer Bonus Bilt points transfer to JetBlue at 1:1. This December announcement doesn’t include a bonus on those transfers. I’m generally not moving Bilt points to JetBlue for ordinary redemptions worth around 1.3 cents apiece. One option worth comparing is a regular paid JetBlue ticket purchased through Bilt’s portal using points. Under ordinary revenue-ticket rules, that should earn tiles, whereas transferring points into TrueBlue doesn’t earn tiles. Portal bookings do give up JetBlue’s direct-booking points bonus. The more interesting transfer uses remain partner business class awards, such as the 54,000-point Condor business class awards from the East Coast to Frankfurt I’ve covered, when available. Mosaic doesn’t add benefits to a Condor flight. If you already have the JetBlue Premier card, its 15% award rebate includes partner flights. A 54,000-point award returns 8,100 TrueBlue points, for a net cost of 45,900. You need all 54,000 upfront, and the rebate comes back as JetBlue points, not Bilt points. A 100% Statement Credit Bonus Still Only Gets You About 1.1 Cents Eligible cardholders get increased statement credit redemption value from November 20 at 9 a.m. Eastern through December 2 at 2:59 a.m. Eastern. The minimum redemption is 1,000 points. This bonus depends on which Bilt credit card you have, not your Bilt elite status. At the usual 0.55-cent statement credit redemption rate, the math is: Bilt Card   Bonus   Value Per Point   Credit For 10,000 Points Blue 25% 0.6875 cents $68.75 Obsidian 50% 0.825 cents $82.50 Palladium 100% 1.1 cents $110 I wouldn’t do this. Even Palladium’s doubled rate is less than the $125 in travel those same 10,000 points buy through Bilt, before considering Hyatt or airline transfers. I passed on last month’s gift card bonus, too. Two Separate Opportunities To Earn 1,000 Extra Points Some cardholders will receive a targeted offer for 1,000 bonus points after $500 in everyday purchases from November 20 at 9 a.m. Eastern through November 30 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern. Rent and mortgage payments don’t count. Check your account for eligibility. Then the usual Rent Day double points apply on December 1, with a cap of 1,000 additional points: Bilt Blue: 2 points per dollar on everyday spending. Bilt Obsidian: 6 points in your selected dining or grocery category, 4 on travel and 2 on other everyday spending. Bilt Palladium: 4 points per dollar on everyday spending. Rent and tax payments don’t qualify for the extra points (tax payments usually don’t earn at all). On Palladium, $500 in eligible December 1 spending earns the full 1,000-point Rent Day bonus on top of the usual 1,000 points. The holiday shopping offer ends the night before Rent Day. The same purchase can’t satisfy both offers. A targeted Palladium member with $500 of ordinary spending before the deadline and another $500 on December 1 could earn 2,000 promotional bonus points across the two. Brittany Snow, Free Rent And December Experiences Brittany Snow is this month’s Rent Free guest. The game opens November 20 at noon Eastern and closes December 1 at 3 p.m. Eastern, with results after 4 p.m. The top 10 members win a month’s rent up to $2,500, with additional rent winners depending on how well she does. Rent winners also get a signed copy of September Letters. The next 100 receive 1,000 points and the next 500 receive 100 points. There’s also a November 22 brunch with Snow and September Letters co-founder Jaspre Guest at The Twenty Two in New York, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. It’s $45 or 3,000 points, includes bites and cocktails, and opens for booking November 20 at 9 a.m. Eastern. Guests must be at least 21. The booking is final sale. The book itself is $20 or 2,000 points, with 100 copies available beginning November 20 at 9 a.m. Eastern. Members can apply up to $20 of their monthly Bilt Cash allowance. I’d use available Bilt Cash rather than redeem points at a penny each. Shipping is expected in two to three weeks, and sales are final. Members can write letters through the app, choosing whether to keep them private or share them. Select Bilt Alliance buildings will also have September Letters mailboxes, with letters mailed back to their writers in a year. Bookings for the following experiences open Saturday, November 21 at 11:50 a.m. Eastern for Gold and Platinum, and noon for everyone else: Dining: December 1 meals at 40 restaurants across nine cities. Most cost $35–$78 or 2,500–5,000 points. There are three-course menus at most venues, four courses at Hutong and omakase at seven Bondi locations. Drink add-ons cost $20–$46 and must be purchased when booking. Up to $50 Bilt Cash can be applied to one dining experience, with the rest paid in cash. Book by November 30 at 5 p.m. Eastern. There’s also first access to American Cut’s December 31 cocktail party in New York at 6 p.m., priced at $250, with 20 seats. Comedy: 20 demonstrates December 4–19. Club experiences cost $40 or 2,500 points, except Mic Drop MANIA in Chandler at $30 or 2,000 points, with two drinks included. Premium experiences cost $75 or 5,000 points and include two drinks and light bites. Austin’s The Creek & The Cave is among the venues. Members can use up to $50 Bilt Cash toward a comedy show for the month. Booking closes at 11 a.m. Eastern on the show date, or when sold out. Fitness: Free December 1 SoulCycle and Barry’s classes, with 1,175 and 580 spots respectively. Bookings close November 30 at 7 p.m. Eastern. Dining allows four seats per member per booking, and comedy allows four tickets per person. These experiences are final sale. I’d use Bilt Cash before points: a common $60 dinner costs 4,000 points, but applying $50 Bilt Cash leaves $10 to pay and keeps your points available for travel. And on December 1, Bilt’s cafe at 837 Washington Street in New York will offer members a complimentary Daniel Boulud tasting from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern: lobster vol-au-vent (with a vegetarian option), warm apple chausson, a hot chocolate shake and warm spiced cider. Then the usual Rent Day double points apply on December 1, with a cap of 1,000 additional points: Bilt Blue: 2 points per dollar on everyday spending. Bilt Obsidian: 6 points in your selected dining or grocery category, 4 on travel and 2 on other everyday spending. Bilt Palladium: 4 points per dollar on everyday spending. Rent and tax payments don’t qualify for the extra points (tax payments usually don’t earn at all). On Palladium, $500 in eligible December 1 spending earns the full 1,000-point Rent Day bonus on top of the usual 1,000 points. The holiday shopping offer ends the night before Rent Day. The same purchase can’t satisfy both offers. A targeted Palladium member with $500 of ordinary spending before the deadline and another $500 on December 1 could earn 2,000 promotional bonus points across the two. Brittany Snow, Free Rent And December Experiences Brittany Snow is this month’s Rent Free guest. The game opens November 20 at noon Eastern and closes December 1 at 3 p.m. Eastern, with results after 4 p.m. The top 10 members win a month’s rent up to $2,500, with additional rent winners depending on how well she does. Rent winners also get a signed copy of September Letters. The next 100 receive 1,000 points and the next 500 receive 100 points. There’s also a November 22 brunch with Snow and September Letters co-founder Jaspre Guest at The Twenty Two in New York, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. It’s $45 or 3,000 points, includes bites and cocktails, and opens for booking November 20 at 9 a.m. Eastern. Guests must be at least 21. The booking is final sale. The book itself is $20 or 2,000 points, with 100 copies available beginning November 20 at 9 a.m. Eastern. Members can apply up to $20 of their monthly Bilt Cash allowance. I’d use available Bilt Cash rather than redeem points at a penny each. Shipping is expected in two to three weeks, and sales are final. Members can write letters through the app, choosing whether to keep them private or share them. Select Bilt Alliance buildings will also have September Letters mailboxes, with letters mailed back to their writers in a year. Bookings for the following experiences open Saturday, November 21 at 11:50 a.m. Eastern for Gold and Platinum, and noon for everyone else: Dining: December 1 meals at 40 restaurants across nine cities. Most cost $35–$78 or 2,500–5,000 points. There are three-course menus at most venues, four courses at Hutong and omakase at seven Bondi locations. Drink add-ons cost $20–$46 and must be purchased when booking. Up to $50 Bilt Cash can be applied to one dining experience, with the rest paid in cash. Book by November 30 at 5 p.m. Eastern. There’s also first access to American Cut’s December 31 cocktail party in New York at 6 p.m., priced at $250, with 20 seats. Comedy: 20 shows December 4–19. Club experiences cost $40 or 2,500 points, except Mic Drop MANIA in Chandler at $30 or 2,000 points, with two drinks included. Premium experiences cost $75 or 5,000 points and include two drinks and light bites. Austin’s The Creek & The Cave is among the venues. Members can use up to $50 Bilt Cash toward a comedy show for the month. Booking closes at 11 a.m. Eastern on the show date, or when sold out. Fitness: Free December 1 SoulCycle and Barry’s classes, with 1,175 and 580 spots respectively. Bookings close November 30 at 7 p.m. Eastern. Dining allows four seats per member per booking, and comedy allows four tickets per person. These experiences are final sale. I’d use Bilt Cash before points: a common $60 dinner costs 4,000 points, but applying $50 Bilt Cash leaves $10 to pay and keeps your points available for travel. And on December 1, Bilt’s cafe at 837 Washington Street in New York will offer members a complimentary Daniel Boulud tasting from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern: lobster vol-au-vent (with a vegetarian option), warm apple chausson, a hot chocolate shake and warm spiced cider. Topics on this pageBilt RewardsFrequent-flyer programJetBlueTrueBlueCondorFrankfurtHyattNew YorkPremium economy classSnowUnited Airlines+7 more More From View from the Wing.

    The immediate value is better seating and fewer fees on trips you already intend to take.

    Main Base fares exclude key seating benefits. And Mosaic 1 through 3 don’t include Mosaic 4 lounge access.

    In a recent development, jetBlue has also announced complimentary upgrades to its latest BlueFirst domestic first class for all Mosaic tiers as equipped aircraft enter service. These are space available upgrades, with higher Mosaic levels ahead of lower ones. Main Base and EvenMore Base fares don’t qualify.

    Industry observers note that premium Upgrade Certificates can confirm Mint or BlueFirst, including on eligible TrueBlue points tickets. Four certificates don’t necessarily mean four upgrades because the number required varies by flight.

    Starting February 1, JetBlue will also let Mosaic 2 members select a certificate through Perks You Pick. I’ve asked whether matched members get that selection.

    Under JetBlue’s Blue Sky partnership, Mosaic members receive benefits on eligible United Airlines trips booked through JetBlue, including a checked bag, preferred seats after booking and Economy Plus at check-in. Mosaic 1 gets Group 2 boarding, while Mosaic 2 and above get Group 1. United flights booked through JetBlue also earn tiles under the ordinary program. So you can keep JetBlue status through travel on United. There’s No Transfer Bonus Bilt points transfer to JetBlue at 1:1. This December announcement doesn’t include a bonus on those transfers. I’m generally not moving Bilt points to JetBlue for ordinary redemptions worth around 1.3 cents apiece. One option worth comparing is a regular paid JetBlue ticket purchased through Bilt’s portal using points. Under ordinary revenue-ticket rules, that should earn tiles, whereas transferring points into TrueBlue doesn’t earn tiles. Portal bookings do give up JetBlue’s direct-booking points bonus. The more interesting transfer uses remain partner business class awards, such as the 54,000-point Condor business class awards from the East Coast to Frankfurt I’ve covered, when available. Mosaic doesn’t add benefits to a Condor flight. If you already have the JetBlue Premier card, its 15% award rebate includes partner flights. A 54,000-point award returns 8,100 TrueBlue points, for a net cost of 45,900. You need all 54,000 upfront, and the rebate comes back as JetBlue points, not Bilt points. A 100% Statement Credit Bonus Still Only Gets You About 1.1 Cents Eligible cardholders get increased statement credit redemption value from November 20 at 9 a.m. Eastern through December 2 at 2:59 a.m. Eastern. The minimum redemption is 1,000 points. This bonus depends on which Bilt credit card you have, not your Bilt elite status. At the usual 0.55-cent statement credit redemption rate, the math is: Bilt Card   Bonus   Value Per Point   Credit For 10,000 Points Blue 25% 0.6875 cents $68.75 Obsidian 50% 0.825 cents $82.50 Palladium 100% 1.1 cents $110 I wouldn’t do this. Even Palladium’s doubled rate is less than the $125 in travel those same 10,000 points buy through Bilt, before considering Hyatt or airline transfers. I passed on last month’s gift card bonus, too.     ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • India turned its population bomb into a demographic dividend; surely its polluted air deserves the same rebranding.
    • A few mornings ago, I landed in Delhi and caught the city’s signature scent outside the airport.
    • Those of us who grew up in India and moved abroad remember misty winter mornings fondly.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Photo Credit: Pollution tourism by Grok.

    India turned its population bomb into a demographic dividend; surely its polluted air deserves the same rebranding.

    A few mornings ago, I landed in Delhi and caught the city’s signature scent outside the airport. In the Uber to my hotel, people were out on their morning walks, exercising in thick smog. I barely saw a mask. The tourism ministry should have been filming.

    Those of us who grew up in India and moved abroad remember misty winter mornings fondly. Delhi has thoughtfully made the mist available all day. Luxury hotels spend fortunes inventing signature fragrances. Delhi has one that arrives with the airport transfer, free of charge.

    Someone should be selling this. I propose…pollution tourism.

    In 1968, biologist Paul Ehrlich opened The Population Bomb with a taxi ride through Delhi on “one stinking hot night,” past crowded streets and through a haze of dust and smoke. He forecast mass famine. For decades, India’s population was described as a bomb. Today, with much of the developed world aging,.

    #7181. Tech Report: American Airlines Hasn’t Flown To Israel Since October 7—Now It’s Partnering With The Airline Flying Its Old Jets

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: American Airlines Hasn’t Flown To Israel Since October 7—Now It’s Partnering With The Airline Flying Its Old Jets

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2537 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • American Airlines hasn’t flown to Israel since the October 7, 2023 attacks.
    • In August I flagged that Israir had acquired American’s old aircraft.
    • Israir presently flies five times a week between New York JFK and Tel Aviv.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    American Airlines hasn’t flown to Israel since the October 7, 2023 attacks. Israir is flying the route using two of American’s retired Airbus A330s. Now American is partnering with Israir to connect those passengers to its network beyond Upcoming York. In August I flagged that Israir had acquired American’s old aircraft. Now it’s getting access to more of the customers it needs to fill those planes. American, meanwhile, gets connecting passengers and an Israeli sales partner ahead of its own planned return to the Israel market. Israir currently flies five times a week between New York JFK and Tel Aviv. American plans to resume daily service March 27, 2027, using Boeing 777-200ERs. I’d covered their previous plan to return in March 2026, they’ve kept planning to return and then not, given instability in the region even as other U.S. carriers flew. Ex-American Airlines Airbus A330-200 N287AY, Credit: Anna Zvereva / Wikimedia Commons.” What American And Israir Have Agreed To The initial arrangement has two parts: Israir will put its flight code on American’s JFK–Tel Aviv service. Israir can market an American-operated flight as part of its own offering when American returns. An interline agreement will connect passengers beyond JFK. Travelers crossing the Atlantic on either airline will be able to combine that flight with American connections across the United States, Canada, Latin America and the Caribbean. An interline agreement supplies the framework for selling a connecting trip on one ticket and through-checking bags. A codeshare adds another airline’s flight number to the same flight. The initial codeshare involves Israir marketing American’s flight. American hasn’t announced that it’s putting its code on Israir’s A330 service. Israir’s stock exchange filing indicates the agreement was signed November 19, with initial implementation targeted by the end of 2026. That depends on regulatory approvals, technology and operational readiness. Israir Airbus A320, Credit: Oyoyoy via Wikimedia Commons Israir Sees A $20–40 Million Revenue Opportunity Until now, Israir’s New York route has competed primarily for passengers whose destination is New York. American connections let it compete for people going beyond New York as well. Israir estimates that this expands its potential customer market by 20–25%, creating an opportunity for $20–40 million in additional annual revenue. The filing though describes this as the larger addressable market rather than a revenue growth forecast. A codeshare on American’s flight also gives it something to sell when its own flight isn’t operating or its seats are full. For American, the near-term benefit is carrying Israir passengers on flights it’s already operating beyond JFK. Once American returns to Tel Aviv, Israir can also help sell seats on that flight through its own customer base and distribution in Israel. El Al And Delta Already Have A More Complete Partnership American is playing catch-up in Israel. Delta restored daily JFK–Tel Aviv service in September, and United returned that month as well. El Al and Arkia also serve the New York market. United can combine its Tel Aviv flying with its Newark hub. El Al has a Delta relationship that includes reciprocal codeshares, mileage earning and redemption, and elite benefits. That partnership began in 2024. What Passengers Get—And What They Don’t The immediate customer proposition is an easier connecting itinerary once the agreement goes live. Israir operates out of American’s JFK Terminal 8, so passengers won’t need to change terminals (and terminals aren’t connected airside at JFK). Passengers arriving from Israel still need to clear U.S. immigration and customs. Checking a bag through to the final destination doesn’t eliminate collecting and rechecking it on arrival in the United States. American also confirms Greenwich Lounge access at JFK for passengers flying Israir business class. However, there are no AAdvantage mileage earning, Loyalty Points, award redemptions or reciprocal elite benefits on Israir. The airlines say they’ll consider broader codesharing and AAdvantage benefits later. Hopefully status-earning and award redemption on Israir comes to fruition in the future. American also confirms Greenwich Lounge access at JFK for passengers flying Israir business class. However, there are no AAdvantage mileage earning, Loyalty Points, award redemptions or reciprocal elite benefits on Israir. The airlines say they’ll consider broader codesharing and AAdvantage benefits later. Hopefully status-earning and award redemption on Israir comes to fruition in the future.     Until now, Israir’s Upcoming York route has competed primarily for passengers whose destination is New York. American connections let it compete for people going beyond New York as well.

    Israir estimates that this expands its potential customer market by 20–25%, creating an opportunity for $20–40 million in additional annual revenue. The filing though describes this as the larger addressable market rather than a revenue growth forecast. A codeshare on American’s flight also gives it something to sell when its own flight isn’t operating or its seats are full.

    For American, the near-term benefit is carrying Israir passengers on flights it’s already operating beyond JFK. Once American returns to Tel Aviv, Israir can also help sell seats on that flight through its own customer base and distribution in Israel.

    In a recent development, american is playing catch-up in Israel. Delta restored daily JFK–Tel Aviv service in September, and United returned that month as well. El Al and Arkia also serve the New York market. United can combine its Tel Aviv flying with its Newark hub. El Al has a Delta relationship that includes reciprocal codeshares, mileage earning and redemption, and elite benefits. That partnership began in 2024.     Turkey earned 5% more from tourism in the third quarter from 1% fewer visitors, but hotels aren’t the ones capturing the gain.

    Culture and tourism minister Mehmet Ersoy credited the rise in tourism revenue, captured by the Turkish Statistical Institute, to “longer stays and higher overnight spending.”.

    Recent findings suggest that average visitor stays stood at 10.7 nights in the third quarter, up from 10.2 a year earlier. Spending per night rose 6.7% to $107, lifting total spending per visitor by about 12% to $1,145.

    But hotel rates don’t explain the gain in tourist spending. In dollar terms, average rates fell fractionally to $148 a night in Q3, down from $149 last year, according to Lighthouse.

    Package tour expenditures accounted for 32.3% of total tourism income, followed by food and beverage spending at 20.5% and accommodation at 12.5%, the Turkish Statistical Institute data revealed.

    • Martin Solar‘s newly manufactured Dual-Channel Solar Rail (DCSR) was recently installed on a 70-kWDC solar project, marking its first real-world application.
    • Sources indicate that “Management of PV wires and AC trunk cables is one of the most notable aspects of rooftop PV installation.
    • DCSR is designed with a wire trough large enough to fit three-phase trunk cables, like those manufactured by Enphase, Hoymiles, and AP Systems.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Martin Solar‘s newly manufactured Dual-Channel Solar Rail (DCSR) was recently installed on a 70-kWDC solar project, marking its first real-world application.

    The Dual-Channel Solar Rail from Martin Solar.

    Sources indicate that “Management of PV wires and AC trunk cables is one of the most notable aspects of rooftop PV installation. Anyone who has ever experienced running hundreds, thousands of feet of conductors on a rooftop system knows what a hassle it is having to apply countless zip ties that are not really suitable for long-term wire management,” noted Preston Nelson, director of Martin Solar and co-inventor of DCSR. “What’s worse than the initial application of zip ties is having to pull up finished solar panels to apply even more zip ties after an inspector inevitably cites an installation for having wires that droop down to the roof surface.”.

    DCSR is designed with a wire trough large enough to fit three-phase trunk cables, like those manufactured by Enphase, Hoymiles, and AP Systems. It can also fit up to twenty standard PV cables, without the use of zip ties. Instead of using specialized panel clamps, DCSR’s panel attachment channel is off to the side of the wire trough, where it separately accepts panel hardware.

    Industry observers note that “The dual-channel design with separately dedicated features allowed us to increase the cross-sectional area of the wire trough to a size never seen before as a rail feature. In the past, we would install a separate wire tray to manage numerous long trunk cable runs, which was even more expensive and time-consuming. Now, this present project installation involves over 600 total feet of trunk, without a single cable tie. The separate wire trough can even allow access to wire runs without lifting panels, especially convenient when a worker simply needs to track a PV string,” Nelson mentioned.

    DCSR is the first product accessory to Martin Solar’s Hidden-Fastener Solar Mount, which mounts to the roof surface without putting holes in shingles. While Martin’s proprietary solar rail and mount can be paired, both are compatible with other solar racking and mounts.

    Martin Solar will show DCSR and its solar mounting system at RE+ from November 17 to 19 at booth C5071.

    Travelers Want Less Screen Time and More Time on the Water

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Travelers are moving from talking about getting outside to booking experiences that take them there.
    • This sponsored content was created in collaboration with a Skift partner.
    • Recent findings suggest that people have spent years saying they want to spend less time on their screens.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Travelers are moving from talking about getting outside to booking experiences that take them there. New research from Boatsetter points to growing participation in outdoor and water-based activities, creating opportunities for hospitality brands to make shared experiences more accessible.

    This sponsored content was created in collaboration with a Skift partner.

    Recent findings suggest that people have spent years saying they want to spend less time on their screens. Now more of them are acting on it. Boatsetter, a booking platform for boat sharing and on-water experiences, tracks that shift in its new report, Great Outdoor Shift 2.0. The report draws on two online surveys of U.S. adults: 834 in December 2025 and 1,034 in September 2026.

    Boatsetter’s 2026 Great Outdoor Shift survey shows people responding to digital overload: 77% of respondents said they had already reduced screen time and social media use, and 63% said they would trade screen time for time on or near the water. The pull is about well-being, too: 84% say the outdoors is vital for their mental health.

    “People aren’t just tired of their screens. They want something that makes them feel small and present. That’s what awe does, and it’s why time on the water with friends keeps topping the list of what Americans want most,” remarked Michael Farb, CEO of Boatsetter.

    Recent findings suggest that comparing the two surveys, Boatsetter reports a 64% increase in the number of people who tried fishing or paddlesports, a sign that participation is growing. Research from Tripadvisor supports this: In the first half of 2026, U.S. bookings on Tripadvisor grew 57% for fishing charters and 37% for boat rentals compared with the same period in 2025, according to the company’s 2026 Mid-Year Experiences Trends Report.

    For hotels, destinations, and other travel providers, the figures point to demand for experiences that bring people into a destination, not just around it.

    Sources indicate that boatsetter’s research also points to a broader shift toward active, social travel. Time on the water with friends remains the experience respondents most want more of. Spending intent is rising, too: 82% plan to spend more on outdoor or water activities in 2027, and 37.5% of this year’s respondents want to spend significantly more, compared with 23.4% in Boatsetter’s 2025 survey. For hospitality brands, the practical opportunity lies in helping guests discover and book experiences, from guided excursions to activities with local operators.

    Recent findings suggest that the pull toward the outdoors extends beyond water activities. Hilton’s 2026 Trends Report, based on a survey of 14,009 adults in 13 countries who plan to travel in the next 12 months, found that rest and recharging is the top motivation for leisure travel, cited by 56% of respondents. Spending time in nature was also among their top desires, with 37% citing it as such. Both findings point to demand for experiences that help travelers step away from routine.

    Great Outdoor Shift 2.0 explores three questions for travel and hospitality leaders:.

    It has been revealed that taken together, the findings point to a role for travel companies that goes beyond providing a view of nature. In 2027, hotels, tourism boards, and travel partners can make shared outdoor activities easier to access through local partnerships, clearer booking options, and experiences suited to different interests. The opportunity is to help guests follow through on the time they already say they want outdoors.

    According to recent reports, “We’ve known the desire to get outside is there. What’s changing is that people are acting on it, and they expect technology to help, not get in the way. Our job is to make the outdoor experiences they want easy to reach,” Farb remarked.

    Tech Report: The Complex Reputation of James Burnham

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (236 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The British first edition of The Managerial Revolution that I picked up in a Charing Cross Road shop a quarter century ago tells us much about the work itself.
    • Industry observers note that burnham, who entered the world 121 years ago Sunday and left it nearly 40 years ago, very much remains part of the Great Conversation.
    • Flynn, the author of The Man Who Invented Conservatism: The Unlikely Life of Frank S.

    The British first edition of The Managerial Revolution that I picked up in a Charing Cross Road shop a quarter century ago tells us much about the work itself. I’ve read it four times, conscripted it as an airplane companion, and brought it to the beach. Yet its binding remains strong, its cover quite flexible, and its pages yellowing but intact. We no longer much refer to let alone read such 1941 bestsellers as Clifton Fadiman’s Reading I’ve Liked or Margaret Leech’s Reveille in Washington. But James Burnham, much like my strong and solid copy of his most famous book, endures.

    Industry observers note that burnham, who entered the world 121 years ago Sunday and left it nearly 40 years ago, very much remains part of the Great Conversation. The Managerial Revolution, anticipating as it did the ascension of technocrats, specialists, and the bureaucratic elite as a sort of ruling class, surely helped in that regard. Burnham remains read, despite no Burnhamite clique in academia or organized faction among movement conservatives dedicated to advancing his ideas. Kirkians, Straussians, and Randians exist. Why no James Burnham Preservation Society with an accompanying secret handshake?

    Daniel J. Flynn, the author of The Man Who Invented Conservatism: The Unlikely Life of Frank S. Meyer, is an American Spectator senior editor, visiting fellow at the Hoover Institution, and YouTuber @RightWingWilderness.

    On “The Complex Reputation of James Burnham”.
